title: Origins: Oncogenesis
description: A cancer is not one mistake but several: an oncogene stuck on, a tumour suppressor like p53 lost, a checkpoint skipped - each a mutation that gives one cell an advantage over its neighbours. The hallmarks of cancer are what that cell has learned. Unlocks the Anomalous Strain Culture.

puzzle.goal: A cell becomes malignant only after n separate rare mutations, in a fixed order, each happening at a small constant rate k_j per year. The chance that a single cell has collected all n by age t is the product of the rates times the volume of the ordered region of mutation times inside [0, t]. Write the yearly incidence of the disease at age t: the derivative of that chance.
puzzle.name: Armitage–Doll multistage model of carcinogenesis
puzzle.ask: Most cancers fit about six stages. With every k_j = k per year and n = 6, find the incidence at age t, in cases per 100,000 people per year (it rises as the fifth power of age - as measured).

vars.k: mutation rate of a stage (per year)

puzzle.method: The n mutation times t₁ < t₂ < ... < t_n inside [0, t] fill a simplex of volume tⁿ/n!. Multiply by the rates and differentiate in t.
